# **Validating Your World: Files and App Data (Start Here)**

## **👉 WATCH THIS\!**

| World Creation Walkthrough | \~11 mins | 📹[World Creation Walkthrough](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JYbUu6vnQjNcfwpqg-ygC-7oRdSEXqS3/view?usp=drive_link) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

## 

## **The big idea: the AI reviewer holds your Canonical Values tab as the answer key**

The pipeline (the automated system that builds your world) has finished. It handed you a stack of documents and a set of data tables. Your job is to check what it made and fix what it got wrong, so the world passes QC.

One idea runs through this whole guide. When the pipeline finishes, an automated checker (we call it "the AI reviewer") opens your World Spec Document and reads the **"(3) Facts & Traps"** tab as the answer key. For every row it records four things:

* The **Key** (FT001, FT002, and so on)  
* The **Type** (Grounding fact, or Trap)  
* The **Value** (the exact fact or number the world must carry)  
* Where it should **Appear**

That tab is your **Facts and Traps ledger**. The reviewer checks the world the pipeline built against it. Everything else in this guide makes the world match the ledger.

Here is how the reviewer judges each row:

* **Grounding fact** (Type \= Grounding fact): the world MUST carry this exact Value, the same everywhere it appears. If two files disagree, or any value contradicts the registered Value, that is a REAL DEFECT and the world FAILS. The report names the FT\#\#\# and the Value it expected.  
* **Trap** (Type \= Trap): the inconsistency is on purpose. The reviewer leaves it alone ONLY if it maps to an FT\#\#\# Trap row you wrote down. "It might be intentional" is not enough. If you did not register it as a Trap with a Key, the reviewer treats the mismatch as a defect.

This grounding is additive. All the consistency checks below still run. Each one is now judged against your ledger.

### What the AI reviewer hands you back

When the AI reviewer finishes, it gives you a **fix-list**. This is its report. Read it top to bottom. Each line names the file, the problem it found, and (when the problem maps to a fact you registered) the FT\#\#\# Key and the Value it expected. A line looks like this:

| `[FAIL] FT002 Numerical consistency file: q3_financials.xlsx  Expected annual revenue $140M (registered grounding fact), found $135M. Fix the file to match.` |
| :---- |

Not every line carries an FT\#\#\# Key. Some flags are general (for example, "this file looks empty" or "this date is in the future"). For those, the line still names the file and the problem, and you check it against your ledger yourself. You will see exactly where this fix-list appears in the next section.

## **The Golden Rule**

| App data is authoritative over files unless the fact is a Trap. |
| :---- |

The app data is the source of truth. Every file must reconcile to (agree with) the app data. When a file and the app data disagree, fix the file, not the app data, unless you registered that exact mismatch as a Trap.

This rule has a direction, and the direction matters. When a file and the app data fight, you almost always change the FILE. You leave the app data alone. The one exception is a registered Trap. You will see this play out in the worked example below (see "When a file and the app data disagree").

## **Your two jobs**

You are the worldbuilder. You have two jobs at this stage.

1. **Make every grounding fact match.** Make every grounding fact appear with its registered Value, the same everywhere, across both the files and the app data. Fix anything the pipeline got wrong, let drift, or made up.  
2. **Make sure every intended mismatch is registered as a Trap.** A Trap is an inconsistency you put in the world on purpose. The reviewer ignores it only if it maps to an FT\#\#\# Trap row you wrote down. A clever mismatch that is not in the ledger does not read as clever. It reads as a defect. If you find an intended trap you never logged, go back to the spec's Facts and Traps tab and add a row with all four fields: the Key (FT\#\#\#), Type \= Trap, the Value, and where it appears.

**A Trap row only works if it is specific.** The reviewer has to MATCH the exact mismatch in the world to the exact Trap row you wrote. The Trap's Value and its "where it appears" must be specific enough to bind to one real mismatch. A vague Trap row does not bind, and the mismatch still fails.

* **Bad Trap row:** Value \= "some numbers may differ." (Too vague. The reviewer cannot tell which mismatch this covers, so it does not suppress anything.)  
* **Good Trap row:** Value \= "Q3 deck shows $11.0M while Q3 invoices sum to $10.4M." Where it appears \= "Q3 board deck vs Q3 invoice set." (Specific. The reviewer can bind the exact in-world mismatch to it and leave it alone.)

## **Same review, two file sets, in order**

You run the same review twice, on two sets of files.

* **Stage 1: the FILE SYSTEM.** These are the documents the pipeline wrote: Word files, spreadsheets, decks, PDFs.  
* **Stage 2: the APP DATA.** These are the CSV tables the pipeline builds FROM your finished files. (A CSV is a simple table saved as plain text, one row per line.)

Both stages are grounded in the same Facts and Traps ledger.

Because the app data is built from the files, **fix the files first.** Once the app data has been generated, you do NOT regenerate it when you patch a file. You hand-correct the app data directly so it stays consistent. (The pipeline can be re-run as a separate, deliberate action, but that is not part of normal fixing.)

## **A worked example: one worldbuilder, one ledger, side by side**

Picture a worldbuilder named Dana. The pipeline has finished a media-licensing world. Dana opens the generated world on one side of the screen and the spec's **"Canonical Values"** tab on the other. Dana works down the ledger, one row at a time, and treats it as the answer key, exactly the way the AI reviewer will.

**Grounding fact FT004: the world's "now" is May 18, 2026\.** (The "now" anchor is the single date the world is frozen at. Nothing in the world can be dated after it.)

Dana opens the export files. Two of them carry a comment, "Rebuilt 2026-05-26." That date is 8 days after the world's "now." A file cannot have been rebuilt on a date that has not happened yet. One of those files even carries two stamps that fight each other: "Export Date: 2026-05-18" and "Rebuilt 2026-05-26." Dana checks the ledger. There is no Trap row for a future rebuild date. So this is a real defect. Dana fixes both files so the stamps read May 18, 2026, and removes the contradiction.

**Grounding fact FT002: annual revenue is $140M.**

Dana looks for the revenue figure everywhere it appears: the financial statement, the model, and the CSV. A clean world keeps a figure like $140M identical in all three. Dana confirms they match. (If even one file had said $120M or $160M, and no Trap row covered it, this would be a numerical-consistency defect, which is a blocking failure.)

**When a file and the app data disagree (the Golden Rule in action).**

Dana finds something trickier. A contract file says annual revenue is $140M, but the accounting app's data table (the source the app loads from) says $135M. The two disagree. Dana checks the ledger: FT002 is registered as a grounding fact with Value $140M, and there is no Trap row for this difference.

Here the Golden Rule decides the fix. App data is authoritative. So Dana does NOT edit the app data table to say $140M. Dana fixes the FILE so it reconciles to (agrees with) the app data. Then Dana checks the registered Value: the ledger says $140M, but the authoritative app data says $135M. That means the ledger or the app data is itself wrong, so Dana resolves the conflict at the source (correct the registered Value or the app data table) and then sets every file to match. Remember: when a file and the app data fight, you change the file, not the app data, unless the mismatch is a registered Trap.

**Grounding fact FT007: the department is named "Information Technology."**

The official master list (the canonical list, meaning the single authoritative version everything else should follow) says "IT." Later files say "Information Technology." Another pair reads "Admin & Ops Support" in one place and "Administration & Operations" in another. No rename memo anywhere in the world shows a name changed on purpose. So the same department wears two names. Dana picks the registered Value and makes every file use it.

* **Bad:** one file says "IT," another says "Information Technology," with nothing explaining the switch.  
* **Good:** every file says "Information Technology," because that is the registered Value. OR a dated in-world memo shows the rename and which name is used after it.

**Document chronology: an invoice dated before its contract.**

Dana checks the order of events. An invoice is dated March 3, but the contract it bills against is dated March 10\. The bill comes before the thing it bills for. That is impossible: the effect lands before its cause. This is not a future-date problem. It is an out-of-order problem. Dana checks the ledger for any Trap covering it, finds none, and fixes the dates so the contract comes first and the invoice comes after.

**Grounding fact FT011: the royalty rates live in Schedule B.**

A master license cites "Schedule B \[on file\]" for royalty rates in 5 or more documents. Dana searches the world for that file. There is no Schedule A or Schedule B file anywhere in the 121-file world. The documents point at something that does not exist. Dana either creates the Schedule B file the documents promise, or removes the references. The fix has to leave the world whole.

**A streaming-usage CSV that looks too clean.**

Dana opens a subscriber CSV. The subscriber counts are exactly 11,000,000 and 7,000,000, flat across all 12 quarters. Revenue is identical every quarter. Stream counts climb by exactly \+8,000,000 each quarter. Real businesses do not move in perfectly round, perfectly even steps. The phone numbers are all "555" numbers. This is machine-clean data. Dana edits the numbers so they vary the way real figures do, and replaces the placeholder phone numbers.

**A contradiction that should have been a Trap.**

Dana finds a Q3 deck showing $11.0M while the invoices for the same quarter sum to $10.4M. That is a real mismatch. Dana checks the ledger. There is no Trap row for it. Dana planned this contradiction as a deliberate test, but never wrote it down.

Here is the key lesson. As it stands, the reviewer will flag it as a numerical-consistency defect, because an unregistered mismatch is a defect. Dana has a choice:

* If the contradiction is meant to be a trap, go to the Facts and Traps tab and add a Trap row: FT021, Type \= Trap, Value \= "Q3 deck shows $11.0M while Q3 invoices sum to $10.4M," where it appears \= "Q3 board deck vs Q3 invoice set." That Value is specific enough for the reviewer to bind the exact mismatch to it, so now the reviewer leaves it alone.  
* If it was an accident, fix the deck or the invoices so they agree.

Dana decides it is a real trap, so Dana adds FT021 to the ledger.

## **Stage 1: File System Checks**

Below are the checks the reviewer runs on the file system, with the ones that matter most first. "Critical" marks a blocking check: it must pass for the world to pass. Every check is judged against your Facts and Traps ledger.

For every flag: read the AI reviewer's fix-list, then open the file yourself and check it against your ledger.

### 1\. Timeline and Dates Are Coherent

Every date must agree with the world's "now" anchor (the single date the world is frozen at) and with the other dates. Nothing can be dated in the future.

* **Bad:** the world's "now" is May 18, 2026, but two export files carry "Rebuilt 2026-05-26," 8 days in the future. One file even has two stamps that fight each other: "Export Date: 2026-05-18" and "Rebuilt 2026-05-26."  
* **Good:** every stamp sits on or before May 18, 2026, and one file carries one consistent date.  
* **Fix:** find every date, compare it to the "now" anchor in your ledger, move any future date back, and remove the contradicting stamp.

### 2\. Document Chronology Is Causally Consistent

Events must run in cause-then-effect order. The cause comes first. The effect comes after. This is not only about future dates. It is about the order of events relative to each other.

* **Bad:** an invoice dated March 3 bills against a contract dated March 10, so the bill exists before the contract it bills for. Or a payment is recorded before the invoice that asks for it. Or an amendment is dated before the original agreement it changes.  
* **Good:** the contract is dated March 10, the invoice that bills against it is dated after that, and the payment is recorded after the invoice.  
* **Fix:** walk the chain of events and make sure each cause is dated before its effect. Reorder or re-date any event that lands out of order.

### 3\. All Numerical Values and Constraints Are Consistent Across the World (critical)

Every grounding-fact number must read the same in every file and every app table. One number that disagrees fails the check, unless you registered that difference as a Trap.

* **Bad:** the annual revenue figure reads $120M in the statement, $140M in the model, and $160M in the CSV. Three files, three numbers, no Trap registered.  
* **Good:** the registered grounding fact (say FT002, Value \= $140M) reads $140M identically in the statement, the model, and the CSV.  
* **Fix:** pull the number's registered Value from your ledger, set every copy to match. If a difference is meant to be there, register it as a Trap with an FT\#\#\# Key that is specific enough to bind to the exact mismatch.

### 4\. Consistent Naming

One person, one department, one entity keeps one name everywhere. A name changes only if the world shows the change happening.

* **Bad:** the canonical list (the single authoritative version) says "IT," later files say "Information Technology," and another pair reads "Admin & Ops Support" against "Administration & Operations," with no memo bridging the change.  
* **Good:** "IT" everywhere. Or a dated rename memo in the world that shows IT became Information Technology, after which the new name is used.  
* **Fix:** pick the one registered name, replace every other version. If a rename is intended, add the in-world document that shows it.

### 5\. Coherence Flag Ratio (critical) and Realism Flag Ratio (critical)

These two are catch-alls. Even when no single problem is fatal, too many small coherence problems, or too many things that just do not look real, will add up and fail the world. Small mismatches are not free. Each one you leave in raises the count toward a fail.

* **Fix:** clear the individual defects below. Fewer small problems means a lower flag ratio.

### 6\. No Synthetic Markers or Placeholder Data

The world must not look machine-made. No data that is too clean. No placeholders. No "TBD." ("Synthetic markers" means data that looks generated, not real.)

* **Bad:** a streaming-usage CSV has subscriber counts of exactly 11,000,000 and 7,000,000, flat across all 12 quarters, identical revenue every quarter, stream counts rising exactly \+8,000,000 every quarter, and "555" phone numbers everywhere.  
* **Good:** subscriber counts wobble quarter to quarter, revenue moves with them, and phone numbers vary.  
* **Fix:** add realistic variation; replace placeholder phone numbers, names, and "TBD" entries with believable values that still match your ledger.

### 7\. In-World vs Out-of-World Separation

World content holds only world content. No author notes. No meta-text. No pointers to anything outside the world.

* **Bad:** a memo carries a leftover note to the author instead of just stating its content.  
* **Good:** the memo states its content plainly, with no note attached.  
* **Fix:** delete every author note, comment, and outside reference from the world content.

### 8\. No Broken Document References

Every document, schedule, exhibit, or appendix that a file cites must actually exist IN THE WORLD. This check is about references INSIDE the world pointing to other things inside the world.

* **Bad:** a master license cites "Schedule B \[on file\]" for royalty rates in 5 or more documents, but no Schedule A or Schedule B file exists anywhere in the 121-file world.  
* **Good:** Schedule B exists as a file, and the royalty rates in it match what the license quotes.  
* **Fix:** list every cited document, confirm each one exists, create the missing file or remove the citation.

### 9\. External Citations Resolve To Real Content (also runs)

This is a different check from No Broken Document References. Number 8 is about references that point INSIDE the world. This one is about citations that point OUTSIDE the world, to real things in the real world (a law, a public standard, a named regulation, a real company filing). When a file cites something external, that thing has to be real and the file has to describe it correctly.

Supplementary material from a real company (a downloaded 10-K, a public filing, a press release) falls under this rule: it must be the genuine document, described and used accurately, never edited to fit your fictional world.

* **Bad:** a contract cites "Section 12 of the Imaginary Data Act of 2024," a law that does not exist; or it cites a real statute but states a rule that statute does not contain.  
* **Good:** every external citation names something real and describes it correctly.  
* **Fix:** check each outside-world citation; correct any made-up reference, or fix the description so it matches the real source.

### 10\. Personnel Names, Titles and Roles Are Consistent (critical)

One person keeps one name, one title, and one role across the whole world, unless the world shows a promotion or transfer.

* **Fix:** set every person's name, title, and role to the one registered value. Add the in-world record if a change is real.

### 11\. File Volume and Format Diversity (critical)

The world needs enough files, and enough kinds of files. Mix Word documents, spreadsheets, decks, and PDFs.

* **Fix:** add the missing file types and bring the file count up to a realistic range for the domain.

### 12\. File Integrity Defect Rate (critical)

Every file must open, and nothing inside it can be empty or cut off.

* **Fix:** open every flagged file and rebuild any that are empty, truncated (cut off), or unopenable.

### A few more checks the reviewer runs (all judged against your ledger)

* **Realistic Document Texture:** a real document has the messiness of a real document (headers, footers, signatures, varied phrasing), not the flat sameness of generated text. Fix: vary phrasing and add the normal furniture of a real document.  
* **Anomaly Detection Catch-All:** a sweep for anything odd that the named checks did not catch. Fix: when it flags something, open the file, decide if it is a real defect or a registered Trap, and act accordingly.  
* **Traceability and Cohesion:** the files should hang together as one coherent world, where related documents connect and tell a consistent story. Fix: make sure related files reference and agree with each other, so the world reads as one place, not a pile of unrelated documents.


## **Stage 2: the app data. Same review of files and revisions**

The app data is checked against your ledger the same way the files are.

| PRESERVE THE FORMAT OF THE CSVs EXACTLY. Keep the exact files and tables, the exact columns in the exact order, and the exact field formats. Any change breaks ingestion. This is the single most important app-data rule. |
| :---- |

## **The fix loop (the same five steps for both stages)**

You run the AI reviewer from your World of Worlds task using the named action for each stage: **Run File System AutoQC** (Stage 1\) and **Run App Data AutoQC** (Stage 2). The action runs the check and then moves the task to a review step, where the fix-list described above is posted.

The five steps are the same for both stages.

- [ ] **Review.** Read the AI reviewer's fix-list. Then open the files yourself and check each one against your Facts and Traps ledger. Use the template below for each flag.  
- [ ] **Remediate.** Remediate means: fix it. Fix every real defect.  
- [ ] **Re-upload.** Put the corrected files back as a Zip revision (a single compressed Zip file holding the whole corrected file set; a revision is a new saved version of that set). Leave a short comment on each file you changed.  
- [ ] **Re-run.** Run the AutoQC again for this stage (**Run File System AutoQC** in Stage 1, **Run App Data AutoQC** in Stage 2). It moves back to the review step with an updated fix-list.  
- [ ] **Apply to Task Files.** The **Apply to Task Files** button is on the same task screen. Clicking it saves your corrected files as the official version the rest of the process uses (the official Task Input Files). You can run it again later: if you find another defect after applying, fix it and click Apply to Task Files again to replace the official version with the newer one. Click it once the reviewer passes, OR once each false positive is documented in the task's comment thread on the platform (the RLS task comments, where RLS is the platform the task lives on), naming the file and the Trap or source that resolves it.

### Step 1 fill-in template (Stage 1, for each flag)

| `Flagged item: _______________________________________ Is it a grounding fact in my spec? Name: ___ Value: __________  -> Does the world match that Value everywhere? [ ] yes [ ] no, fix it Is it an intended trap? [ ] yes -> is it registered with a Canonical Value? Name___  Is the Trap row specific enough to bind to this exact mismatch? [ ] yes [ ] no, make it specific Neither? [ ] -> treat as a real defect and fix it` |
| :---- |

### Step 1 fill-in template (Stage 2, for each table)

| `Table: __________________ CSV file: __________________ Every foreign-key value points to a real row in its target table? [ ] yes [ ] no Field formats correct (e.g. plain date, not datetime)? [ ] yes [ ] no No auto-filled columns included? [ ] yes [ ] no Right app and file set identified? [ ] yes [ ] no Grounding-fact numbers match the ledger Value everywhere? [ ] yes [ ] no` |
| :---- |

### False-positive write-up (use when you pass a flag the reviewer raised)

| `File: __________________ FT### Trap or source that resolves it: __________ Logged in the task comment thread (RLS)? [ ] yes` |
| :---- |

\---

## **Closing checklists**

### World Creation \- File System

- [ ] Every grounding fact appears with its registered Value, the same in every file (checked against the Facts and Traps tab).  
- [ ] Every intentional mismatch is registered as a Trap, specific enough to bind to the exact in-world mismatch.  
- [ ] Dates do not contradict the world's "now" anchor or each other; no future "rebuilt" stamps.  
- [ ] Events run in cause-then-effect order (no invoice before its contract, no payment before its invoice).  
- [ ] Every grounding-fact number reads the same in every file.  
- [ ] Every person, department, and entity keeps one name, unless an in-world rename is shown.  
- [ ] No machine-clean or placeholder data (no perfectly round, perfectly even numbers; no "555" phone numbers; no "TBD").  
- [ ] No author notes or meta-text inside world content.  
- [ ] Every cited document, schedule, exhibit, or appendix actually exists in the world.  
- [ ] Every external citation names a real outside-world source and describes it correctly.  
- [ ] Every person's name, title, and role is consistent everywhere.  
- [ ] Enough files and enough formats (Word, spreadsheets, decks, PDFs).  
- [ ] No empty, truncated, or unopenable files.  
- [ ] Corrected files re-uploaded as a Zip revision, with a comment per changed file.  
- [ ] File System AutoQC re-run and passing (or false positives documented with a thumbs down and comment AND in the task comment thread).  
- [ ] Applied to Task Files.

### World Creation \- App Data and Verification

- [ ] Files were fixed and approved before the app data was generated; after generation, the app data is hand-corrected, never regenerated.  
- [ ] Grounding-fact numbers in the CSVs match the ledger Value everywhere.  
- [ ] Each CSV's columns remain unedited: none deleted, renamed, reordered, or extra.  
- [ ] No auto-filled columns included.  
- [ ] Every file agrees with the app data under the Golden Rule (app data wins unless the fact is a Trap; when they disagree, the file is what you fix).  
- [ ] Corrected app data re-uploaded as a Zip revision, with a comment per changed table.  
- [ ] App Data AutoQC re-run and passing (or false positives documented with a thumbs down and comment AND in the task comment thread).  
- [ ] Applied to Task Files.

When AutoQC passes and you have checked the above, proceed to playground verification (next tab).

# **Validating a World in the Playground**

**Ergon is MCP-first.** Except for Personal Consumer (POC), apps are meant to be used and verified through MCP tools. A web page is not required. For an MCP app with no user interface, the standard and preferred validation path is the Agent inside an RL Studio Playground.

## **The one rule: read the world's records back**

A green schema check, a running service, or a successful tool call does not prove that the world data loaded. You must read the records from the live app and confirm that they are the world's records.

## **MCP-first rule**

1. Standard Ergon app (all non-POC subdomains): Use the app's MCP tools through the Agent in an RL Studio Playground.  
2. Paired MCP \+ UI app: Use the Agent for MCP readback. You may also use the app's UI in the same Playground when visual confirmation is useful.  
3. POC consumer app: POC is the only Ergon subdomain that uses BUA as the primary interaction path. Validate it through the UI in the Playground.

**Important:** The Agent and the UI are validation surfaces, not seed methods. Seeded data must come through the deployed app's supported CSV loader. Do not create, repair, or replace missing seed records through the Agent, the UI, an API, JSON, SQL, or the filesystem. If the records are wrong or missing, return the world to App Data Fixes.

## **Choose the correct Playground surface**

For every assigned app, first check World Information and the Playground connection:

1. MCP tools are present: Open the Agent and validate the app through those tools. This is the required path for non-POC apps, including apps with no screen.  
2. Both MCP tools and a UI are present: Validate through the Agent. You may also open the UI for a second readback, attachments, rendered documents, dashboards, or other visual details.  
3. Only a UI or BUA surface is present: Continue only when the world is in POC. Outside POC, stop and report a wrong-interface or platform configuration issue.

An app marked running is alive, not proven populated. A tool that returns success is connected, not proven populated. The output must show the world's actual records.

## **Login reference for paired UI and POC apps**

Use these Playground credentials only when the app appears in World Information. If a credential does not work, do not guess and do not create a new account. Report the app, platform, and failed login to World Building Ops. The current Playground image takes priority over an older login note.

## **Standard MCP validation: use the Agent**

For every non-POC app, use this workflow in RL Studio:

1. Spawn the Playground from the world-building task and wait until it reaches running.  
2. Open the Agent inside that Playground. Do not leave RL Studio to look for a separate app page.  
3. Ask the Agent to identify the app's available read, list, search, and get-detail tools.  
4. Use the Agent to list the app's records and report the count.  
5. Use the Agent to open at least one named record in full. Check a meaningful field, amount, date, status, attachment, or relationship against the world spec.  
6. Repeat for every assigned app. A multi-app world is not validated until each app has its own readback.  
7. Log the exact records and values that you checked. Do not write only "looks good."

### **Suggested Agent prompt**

`Validate <APP> in this RL Studio Playground using only its MCP tools. First identify the available read, list, search, and get-detail tools. Then list the records and report the count, open <NAMED RECORD> in full, verify <FIELD OR RELATIONSHIP> against the world spec, and report the exact values you found. Do not create, edit, or delete anything.`

A successful response is not enough by itself. The response must show the world's names, counts, and facts. Empty results, demo records, and built-in samples do not pass.

## **Paired MCP \+ UI apps**

A paired app has both MCP tools and a UI. Outside POC, MCP remains the task interaction path. The UI is an additional validation surface; it does not change the Ergon spec to BUA.

Use the Agent first for structured readback. Then use the UI when it gives useful visual proof, such as a rendered PDF, dashboard, attachment, page layout, storefront, or desktop model. Use the login table above.

Do not create missing records in the UI. If the Agent and UI show different data, mark the app NEEDS FIXES and report both results.

## **POC exception: BUA is allowed only here**

Personal Consumer (POC) is the only Ergon subdomain that uses BUA as the primary app interaction path. Open the assigned POC app in the Playground, use the POC login above, and validate the customer-facing surface.

A BUA-only app outside POC is not a normal workaround. Stop and report a platform or task-configuration issue. Do not rewrite the task around the UI.

## **What every readback must prove**

* It is the world's data. Names, companies, people, products, accounts, and documents match the world spec, not the app's samples.  
* The count is sane. The live record count is close to the expected volume and is not zero or a stray handful.  
* A concrete fact matches. Check an amount, date, status, balance, named person, line item, or other exact value.  
* Relationships hold. Open enough detail to confirm links such as order-to-line-item, employee-to-department, invoice-to-customer, document-to-submitter, or task-to-owner.  
* Cross-app facts agree. The same company, person, figure, and date must match in every app and in the filesystem documents.

## **When an app fails**

* **EMPTY:** The service and MCP tools work, but the Agent returns no world records, only demo data, or the wrong values. This is an app-data issue. Return it to App Data Fixes.  
* **BROKEN:** The Playground fails, the app does not start, or the app registers no MCP tools. This is a platform issue. Escalate to World Building Ops.  
* **LOGIN FAILURE:** A paired or POC UI opens, but the documented login fails. Do not create an account. Report the app, platform, image, and credential that failed.  
* **WRONG INTERFACE:** A non-POC app exposes only BUA or a UI and has no MCP tools. Stop and report the configuration issue.

If one world has more than one problem, log each problem separately. Fixing a platform issue does not prove that the app data is present.

## **Reach a verdict**

* **Per app: POPULATED** when the Agent or allowed POC UI reads the world's records, the count is sane, a concrete fact matches, and key relationships hold.  
* **Per app: EMPTY** when the app is reachable but the world data is absent, partial, demo, or wrong.  
* **Per app: BROKEN** when the Playground or app does not start or the expected MCP tools do not register.  
* **Overall: READY FOR TASKING** only when every assigned app passes through the correct interaction path, the filesystem is present, cross-app facts agree, and no data was created manually during validation.  
* **Overall: NEEDS FIXES** when any app is empty, broken, on the wrong interface, inconsistent with another app, or missing a usable login.

Log the verdict and evidence in the RL Studio task comments. When the world is READY FOR TASKING, select Approve Verification / Start Knowledge Transfer.

[**World App Issues Report Form**](https://forms.gle/nyPbnGdt2Fp3o9Z97) 

## **Playground walkthrough checklist**

- [ ] The Playground reached running and every assigned service started.  
- [ ] For every non-POC app, I opened the Agent in the Playground and used the app's MCP tools to read records.  
- [ ] For every paired app, I used the MCP result and, when useful, the UI with the documented login.  
- [ ] For every POC app, I used the BUA/UI path in the Playground and checked the customer-facing surface.  
- [ ] I confirmed the world's names, a sane count, one exact fact, and at least one key relationship per app.  
- [ ] I confirmed that the same people, companies, dates, and figures agree across apps and documents.  
- [ ] I did not create or repair seed data through the Agent, UI, API, JSON, SQL, or filesystem.  
- [ ] I logged each app as POPULATED, EMPTY, or BROKEN, with exact evidence and any interface or login issue.  
- [ ] If every app passed, I selected Approve Verification / Start Knowledge Transfer.

## **Apps**

Julius worlds contain realistic applications that the model can “use” when you request so in your task-writing prompt\!

| Examples of Apps | Real-world equivalents |
| :---- | :---- |
| ERPNext | Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Accounting / Journal Entries |
| Wiki.js | Notion, Asana, Trello |
| DocuSeal | DocuSign |
| SAP SuccessFactors \- Recruiting | SAP SuccessFactors \- Recruiting |
| BambooHR | BambooHR |
| QuickBooks | QuickBooks |
| WooCommerce | WooCommerce |
| Chatwoot | Helpdesk |

## **Apps Requirements** 

Julius is centered around multi-app worlds. Apps are required task surfaces, not background decoration.

1. **Always make sure that your world adheres to the app selection requirements that is pre-seeded in your world**  
   This information is located in “World Information” at the top of the task.

*Example* ↘️  
**![][image30]**

2. **Use apps in every task idea**  
     
   **Single-app world:**  
   Every task idea must require the assigned app.  
     
   **Two-app world:**  
   Every task idea must require both assigned apps.  
     
   **Three-or-more-app world:**  
   Every task idea must require at least two relevant assigned apps.  
     
   **Across the complete idea set:**  
   Every assigned app must be required by at least one task idea.  
     
   **Meaningful Use:**  
   The agent must read information from an app or perform an action in it. Mentioning, opening, or optionally checking an app does not count.  
     
   For each task idea, name the apps and the required action in each.  
     
   Quick test: If an app can be removed and the task still works, the app is not meaningfully used.  
     
   You can use this tool to help you implement apps into your task ideas:  
   [https://ergon-world-app-guide-mercor1.vercel.app/](https://ergon-world-app-guide-mercor1.vercel.app/)   
     
3. **No need to list app files in your world spec**  
   When laying out your world, you only need to incorporate the apps into your task ideas. No need to list the app files. The process is:  
     
- **Spec**: Layout the task ideas with apps that must be used. Layout the files that will be available only  
- **File Generation/Revision**: the spec is used to synthetically create around 50 files for you. You revise to make the data consistent for tasking, and to make sure the files appear natural  
- **App Data Generation**: the files are used to generate the required app files for your world. You do the same as file revision, revising the files for data consistency according to AutoQC

## **World Builder Checklist**

Use this checklist before submitting your world for human review. It turns the standards in this guide — *Depth*, *Realism*, and *Factual Integrity* — into concrete, verifiable steps. If every box below is checked, your world has been built in a way that is compliant with this instruction guide and is ready for review and spawning.

### **Spec**

- [ ] **Standards track declared and marked in the world name** | Every cited code and unit belongs to that track."  
- [ ] **Filled out the basic World Information** | my name and the exact apps for this world, aligning my app selection with the precise guidance received from the *Mercor Ops* team.  
- [ ] **Copied the World Spec Template** | without altering its tab structure, and completed every required section.  
- [ ] **Defined one specific organization** | (industry, size, geography, and operational context) and confirmed the world's center of gravity is *U.S.* jurisdiction (e.g., *U.S. GAAP*, *U.S.* federal & state law, or *U.S.* *HR* and finance regulations); any non-*U.S.* content appears only where genuinely relevant.  
- [ ] **Registered every Threshold** |  each numeric value cited so the spec is the single source of truth for the facts that must reconcile across artifacts.  
- [ ] **Logged my Facts & Traps and Known Issues** | in the spec, with each trap defendable (sequential, recency, seniority-of-source, official-doc-over-email, or a clearly-stated, findable embedded rule) and none that make any task unsolvable.  
- [ ] **Mapped each Fact and Trap** | to the appropriate artifacts in the spec.   
- [ ] **Confirmed enough depth for \~5 tasks** | that failed the model — *50+* file system artifacts planned, plus app data — and kept the spec open as the central registry throughout the build.  
- [ ] **Ran Spec AutoQC** | after clicking *Start Spec AutoQC*, via task status transition (not the in-pipeline *Run AutoQC* button). The run passed — or I documented every false positive in the *RLS* comments and explained my reasoning to the reviewer.  
- [ ] **Passed human review on the spec** | which automatically triggers the *AI* pipeline build of the world.

### **World Creation Checklist (File System)**

- [ ] **Includes 50 file system artifacts** | within the \~*50*  target, with enough substantive content to support *5* tasks that fail the model.  
- [ ] **Used multiple modalities and format diversity** | *Word* documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and *PDFs*.  
- [ ] **Mirrored real organizational folder hierarchies** | (a compliance team files differently than a sales team), so information is deliberately scattered and no single document contains everything an agent needs.  
- [ ] **Populated all facts and traps in the file system** | every *Threshold* registered in the spec appears in the files and reads identically everywhere it surfaces.  
- [ ] **Built defendable traps and human messiness** | (e.g., Final vs. V2.1, conflicting authority resolved by a business rule rather than recency, an amendment buried in a non-obvious source)  
- [ ] **Verified factual integrity world-wide** | every shared name, title, role, number, and date is consistent across all files; there are no broken document references; the chronology is causally coherent; and there are no contradictions.  
- [ ] **Removed synthetic tells** |  no placeholder data, no “as mentioned above,” no generic boilerplate, and no synthetic substitutes for real-world facts; voice, tone, and formatting vary by author and document type, and external citations resolve to real content.  
- [ ] **Remediated every File System AutoQC defect** | after pulling the findings and downloading the world locally — fixing each issue I found and each one *AutoQC* flagged, reuploaded as a new world revision, and commented on what had to be remediated.  
- [ ] **Re-uploaded the file system as a Zip revision** | in the pipeline module, leaving a brief comment on each changed file to help improve the *SyntheGen* pipeline.  
- [ ] **Re-ran File System AutoQC** | from the *Task Action Button* after clicking *Start File System AutoQC*. My most recent *AutoQC* run passed perfectly. If it did not pass perfectly, I commented exactly what the false defects were — naming the file, the design intent (e.g., an intentional trap), or the source that resolves it — in the *RLS* comment section.  
- [ ] **Applied the passing revision to Task Files** | so the *Task Input Files* — the source of truth for all world artifacts — reflect the current file system.

### **World Creation Checklist (App Data & Verification)**

- [ ] **Generated app data from the file system** | using the apps selected at claim time (e.g., *ERPNext*, *BambooHR*, *SAP SuccessFactors*, *DocuSeal*, [*Wiki.js*](http://Wiki.js))  
- [ ] **Confirmed app-plus-files taskability** | Every planned task idea requires the assigned app in a single-app world, both assigned apps in a two-app world, or at least two relevant assigned apps in a three-or-more-app world. Across the full idea set, every assigned app is used at least once. Each task also uses at least two World Files.  
- [ ] **Preserved every app's CSV schema exactly** |  the exact files/tables present, the exact columns, and the exact field formats — making no additions, removals, renames, or format changes.  
- [ ] **Ran the App Data AutoQC review loop** | reviewing the data in *Task Input Files*, downloading it, remediating defects, re-uploading a precise revision, clicking *Start App Data AutoQC*, and re-running until it passed or every false positive is documented and defensible.  
- [ ] **Ran the realism check across apps and files** | — company name, key people and roles, headline financials, contract values, and key dates read the same everywhere they appear; flagged every contradiction and any *AI* tell.

### **Final Check**

- [ ] **Confirmed 5+ judgment-fork tasks that break the model** | each built around a real judgment fork (a rule that lives in the world but is withheld from the prompt, or a profession-correct path a smart generalist would miss) — not merely long step-chains.  
- [ ] **Built the world to one answer** |  domain experts would all land on the same conclusion, the world's own numbers reconcile, and any deliberate mismatch is a denoted trap; if *two* experts could reasonably disagree, the world is too ambiguous, and I fixed it.  
- [ ] **Pinned every key number to one value** |  no ranges and no loose ends, any number appearing in more than one place matches everywhere, and the right answer surfaces in outputs that can be checked.  
- [ ] **Passed all AutoQC checks** | (Spec, File System, and App Data). My most recent *AutoQC* run passed perfectly. If it did not pass perfectly, I commented exactly what the false defects were in the *RLS* comments.  
- [ ] **Applied the latest passing pipeline to Task Files** | the source of truth   
- [ ] **Acknowledged the world is FROZEN after submission** |  no revisions, edits, or additions once production task writing begins — and confirmed it clears the highest bar on *Depth*, *Realism*, and *Taskability* before submitting for human review.
