# **Engineering Domain Help**

## **Section Overview**

This section has been created to help the three engineering domains \- Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical \- to preemptively address and overcome problems that they encounter in their work and task building. This should ease the burden from project staff on Slack and hopefully make your work more efficient

## **General Tips**

**Claude as your LLM Assistant.**  
You should only be using Anthropic’s Claude to help you with your drafting. All of the helper skills that we have built out to make your work faster have been made to work best with Claude. Do not use GPT, do not use Gemini, do not use any LLM other than Claude. 

Make sure to download and import all of the Claude skills that we have developed into your Claude sessions and reference them to make sure that they are present in your context window when you are working. Click [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MheuYbA26NhwoT4MMKn68Pqq27v22YWo?usp=drive_link) for skills repository. 

**AQC Not Running on New Submission?**  
We have identified that there is a latency between using the "Apply revision to task" button and Auto QC recognizing the new filesystem. This means that moving forward, **everyone must wait SEVERAL MINUTES before re-running Auto QC after uploading a revision**. Otherwise, Auto QC will run on your old revision/system and not reflect the changes you've made.

**International standards and Spec AutoQC**  
If a world is intentionally on the International Standards Track (Standards Track \= International), the Spec AutoQC dimension "Concrete, Right-Sized, U.S. Scenario That's Activated" is expected to fail on its U.S.-nexus leg.   
This is a known limitation: the check does not yet read the Standards Track field, and it treats non-U.S. standards (IEC, ISO, Eurocode) or a non-U.S. setting as a missing U.S. scenario, even for a U.S.-based company.   
For a world confirmed as International, disregard a fail on this dimension when it is driven solely by the international standards or the setting, and do not fail the spec on that basis. The other legs still apply: the world must still be concrete, right-sized, and activated by a time-bound catalyst.   
This exception applies only to worlds confirmed International; a U.S.-track world must still meet the U.S. requirement.

## **World Building Tips**

**Building out your file system.**  
The most important thing to realise here is that the aim is not perfection. The aim is to build a world that can successfully host 10 tasks where the cause of model failure will not be a structural world issue but rather task complexity. In other words, the model should not fail because of sloppy file quality, but there is no need to resolve EVERY minor issue. 

## **Task Building Tips**

**Boilerplate prompt templates.** The blocks below are the starting point for every engineering task prompt and the first thing you write. Copy the block for your discipline, replace the bracketed parts with your own request, and keep the Output Specification line exactly as written. Keep the prompt natural per Spec 1B: no step lists, do not name the code or method, and do not tell the model where the trap is. The governing standard lives in the world, not the prompt. State the exact output filename, use at least two world files, and attach a Show Your Work file at submission.

### **Civil / Structural**

**Standards**: (keep these in the world, not the prompt): ASCE 7, ACI 318, AISC 360, AASHTO, IBC for U.S. worlds; Eurocodes and ISO for International worlds. Deliverable: verification or disposition memo (.docx).

**Starter prompt:** (copy, then fill the brackets): \[In one or two natural sentences, state the objective (re-evaluate, verify, reconcile, or disposition) and name the inputs the way an engineer would refer to them, for example 'the latest issued drawings', 'the updated geotech memo', or 'the current project spec'. State the single decision you want back: the governing value, comply or does not comply, or the disposition.\] Return your analysis as a single Word document named \[Exact\_Filename\].docx. Commit to one defensible disposition; do not present multiple branches or hedge between options. State every value with its units, give the governing basis for each conclusion, and do not round intermediate values (report final values to \[N\] decimal places). Produce output reflecting professional engineering standards.

**Make it fail with**: a later authority silently superseding a drawn detail or an earlier calc (an updated memo versus the original), a basis or gate distinction (service versus governing allowable, load gate versus release gate, field-cured versus lab-cured cylinders), or a re-derive-do-not-transcribe requirement.

**Worked example:** (Silverwood, world\_906c1f81f34c4a84a009a31ece5294b2): The updated chloride-source memo for the north abutment is in, and it may change the exposure basis the original durability calc was built on. Re-evaluate the abutment's exposure classification against the current environmental information, and give me the governing exposure class, the required minimum cover, and the maximum water-cementitious ratio. Tell me whether the specified mix and cover still comply, and commit to one answer. Then append the .docx Output Specification line above.

### **Mechanical**

**Standards:** (keep these in the world, not the prompt): ASME for U.S. worlds; ISO for International worlds; plus service references such as ANSI/HI for pumps. Deliverable: verification memo (.docx), or a calc workbook (.xlsx).

**Starter prompt:** (copy, then fill the brackets): \[In one or two natural sentences, state the objective (re-rate, verify, confirm, or disposition) and the inputs an engineer would name, for example 'the vendor submittal', 'the accepted duty point', or 'the current basis of design'. State the single decision you want back: accept, trim, or resubmit, or the governing value. Name any basis to hold fixed.\] Return your analysis as a single Word document named \[Exact\_Filename\].docx. Commit to one defensible disposition; do not present multiple branches or hedge between options. State every value with its units, give the governing basis for each conclusion, and do not round intermediate values (report final values to \[N\] decimal places). Produce output reflecting professional engineering standards**.**

**Make it fail with:** a correction the standard requires but the project never flagged (viscosity, temperature, or altitude), correctly executing a codified method end to end rather than summarizing it, or holding a fixed basis (vendor NPSHr, prior fitting losses) that the model recomputes**.**

**Worked example:** (P-2104, task\_485b9987dbb94876846ce93cca0ce668): We are re-rating pump P-2104 on the heavy gas oil service before we accept the vendor curve. Confirm whether it still meets the hydraulic duty at the actual service viscosity and holds the NPSH margin policy, and tell me whether to accept it, trim the impeller, or send it back for resubmittal. Hold the April fitting-loss basis. Then append the .docx Output Specification line above.

### **Electrical**

**Standards** (keep these in the world, not the prompt): NEC, IEEE, NESC for U.S. worlds; IEC for International worlds. Deliverable: calc workbook (.xlsx) with live formulas, or a review memo (.docx)**.**

**Starter prompt:** (copy, then fill the brackets): \[In one or two natural sentences, state the objective (recheck, size, verify, or disposition) and the inputs an engineer would name, for example 'the panel schedule as installed', 'the drive submittal', or 'the project electrical standard'. State the single decision you want back per item: adequate or inadequate, accept or reject, or the governing value.\] Return your work as a single Excel workbook named \[Exact\_Filename\].xlsx. Build every calculated cell as a live formula (for example \=qty\*rate), not a typed-in result; transcribed or placeholder values will not be accepted. State units in each column header, apply \[rounding rule\], and do not round intermediate values. Give one committed call per line. Produce output reflecting professional engineering standards.

**Make it fail with:** a derating the project never flagged (conductor bundling plus ambient, or continuous-load factor), a re-derive-do-not-transcribe requirement, or a spec value treated as a units or documentation issue when it is a real hardware conflict.

**Worked example** (MCC-3A, task\_98a48083bb4c468594bf780b1a8dae07): Recheck the branch-circuit sizing on MCC-3A as it is actually installed. The exterior location and the shared raceway routing may not match what the schedule was originally sized against, so confirm whether each feeder is still adequate as installed and flag every circuit that is not. Return your work as a single Excel workbook named MCC-3A\_Branch\_Circuit\_Recheck.xlsx with live formulas, ampacity to one decimal, and one adequate or inadequate call per circuit. Then append the rest of the .xlsx Output Specification line above.

### **Pre-submit checklist**

* Prompt is natural: no step list, no code or method named, no trap tell, no 'You are...' opener.  
* Exactly one deliverable, with the exact output filename stated in the prompt.  
* Output Specification line appended (memo or workbook) with the brackets filled.  
* For .xlsx: live formulas required, units in each column header, rounding rule stated, no intermediate rounding.  
* Single committed disposition requested; no hedged branches.  
* The governing standard or procedure lives in an in-world doc, not the prompt.  
* Uses at least two world files; 3 to 8 hours for a domain expert.  
* One trap is live and produces a dramatic failure, not ambiguity or a partial miss.  
* Show Your Work file attached; golden trajectory and required model runs completed.

## **CAD Outputs and Programmatic Verifiers (Pilot)**

### **Pilot status**

Studio can store .FCStd files and run artifact-based database code verifiers against them. CAD tasks are still a controlled pilot, however. Do not publish a CAD task until project staff confirms both that the world uses a FreeCAD-enabled platform and that CAD file types are accepted by the project AutoQC. The current Project Julius P0 file-type allowlist does not include .FCStd. If either gate is missing, stop and escalate; do not rename a CAD file to another extension or substitute screenshots for the model.

Start with native FreeCAD .FCStd deliverables. Do not introduce STEP, STP, STL, IGES, OBJ, or BREP as required outputs until that format has separately been allowlisted, given a task-specific verifier contract, and passed an end-to-end canary.

### **When CAD is appropriate**

Use CAD when the model or geometry is itself a meaningful engineering work product and the task can be judged from objective properties of that artifact. Do not add CAD merely as a visual supplement to a memo or workbook. The task must still be realistic, use in-world evidence, take 3 to 8 hours for a domain expert, and contain one live source of difficulty.

### **Required task setup**

1\. Confirm that the FreeCAD app and FreeCAD MCP tools are available in the task environment before drafting the task. If they are absent, request a FreeCAD-enabled world; do not ask an expert to work around a no-app world.

2\. State the exact output filename in the prompt and enter the identical name in Expected Output Files. For the pilot, use a single .FCStd deliverable saved under filesystem/. State whether the expert is building a new model or revising a supplied seed.

3\. Define the governing units, required named objects or features, dimensions or parameters, tolerances, material or density basis when relevant, and the final engineering decision the artifact must support. Never ask a verifier to infer an unstated tolerance.

4\. If a seed model is supplied, require a different output filename and verify that the output is not a byte-for-byte copy. The task-specific checks must prove the required change, not merely that a valid FCStd file exists.

5\. Upload a genuine .FCStd golden output produced in the same FreeCAD environment. A screenshot, PDF, memo, or renamed archive is not a substitute for the golden CAD file.

6\. When the task requires a parametric model, require real constrained sketches, PartDesign features, spreadsheet aliases, or expression bindings, followed by recompute and save. Custom float properties attached to a single Part::Feature do not by themselves demonstrate parametricity.

### **Minimum verifier bundle**

Every CAD verifier must inspect the final artifact, not the transcript or a claim that the file was created. Use the following core checks, then add task-specific engineering checks:

1\. Output contract and freshness: exact path, filename, extension, non-empty file, and evidence that the output is newly produced rather than a copied input.

2\. FCStd package integrity: valid ZIP container, safe internal paths, readable Document.xml, CRC integrity, embedded BREP presence when a solid is required, and no corrupt or unexpected payloads.

3\. Identity, units, and object structure: required document or component IDs, unit schema, object names and types, visibility, and shape links.

4\. Task-specific dimensions and parameters: exact serialized values, aliases, expressions, and tolerances. Width, length, thickness, clearances, and similar values may be graded when they are explicitly represented in the model.

5\. Geometry and topology records: required solids, faces, edges, shells, volumes, and BREP-level relationships where the FCStd package exposes them reliably.

6\. Revision delta and anti-copy checks: expected additions or changes, cross-file identity, prohibited stale objects, and proof that a supplied seed was meaningfully modified.

7\. Parametric structure, when required: constrained sketches, feature history, spreadsheet aliases, expression bindings, and dependency links. This check should fail a flattened or static impostor even if its nominal dimensions look correct.

8\. Cross-artifact consistency, when another deliverable is explicitly required: model properties must agree with the BOM, calculation workbook, drawing, or memo. Do not add a companion file only to make the verifier easier.

### **Native FreeCAD checks**

Static FCStd parsing does not prove that FreeCAD can open and recompute the model or that the kernel considers the shape valid. Once the version-pinned native grader is enabled in Studio, add checks that open the file in FreeCAD, recompute it, require Shape.isValid(), and read kernel-measured bounding boxes, area, volume, center of mass, inertia, topology, and exportability as relevant to the task.

Do not claim that weight or mass has been verified unless the task provides a trusted material-density basis and the verifier either derives mass from verified volume and density or reads native mass properties. Until the native grader is available, label these properties as not independently verified.

### **Pre-submit CAD checklist**

1\. The world is FreeCAD-enabled and the required CAD extension passes the project file-type gate.

2\. The prompt, Expected Output Files field, golden file, and every verifier use the same exact filename and path.

3\. The golden output scores 100% on every applicable verifier.

4\. At least one negative fixture fails each material check. Include, as applicable, a corrupt package, wrong units, copied seed, flattened/static impostor, wrong dimension, or stale output.

5\. A full Studio trajectory can create, save, upload, and grade the model inside the FreeCAD environment. Local-only success is not sufficient.

6\. A reviewer opens the final artifact, confirms the expected object and feature structure, and verifies that failures are attributable to the task response rather than an app, seed, upload, or grader fault.

7\. Do not weaken a verifier or change metadata merely to turn an infrastructure failure into a pass. Escalate environment and grader failures separately.

## **How to Set Up a CAD Rubric in Studio**

Experts are not expected to invent a secure FCStd parser from scratch. For each CAD task, the expert should first provide a CAD verifier specification using the template below. An approved verifier template or project support can then translate that specification into the DB Code Verifier. Until the reusable templates are published, stop and request help rather than pasting unreviewed code into a rubric row.

### **Information required before creating rubric rows**

Copy and complete this specification for every property you want graded:

**Criterion:** one atomic statement describing exactly one pass condition.

**Why it matters:** the engineering consequence of failure and the source of truth.

**Output artifact:** the exact filesystem/ path and filename of the final .FCStd file.

**Reference artifact:** the exact drawing, specification, BOM, calculation, or seed file that establishes the expected result, including page, sheet, table, or named value where possible.

**Model target:** the exact document, Body, object, feature, sketch constraint, spreadsheet alias, expression, or property that contains the value.

**Expected result:** an exact value, allowed set, relationship, or Boolean condition.

**Units and tolerance:** for example 120.0 mm \+/- 0.1 mm. State whether the tolerance comes from the task, a governing reference, or an approved project default.

**Verifier method:** Static FCStd, Native FreeCAD, or LLM/manual review.

**Priority and weight:** P0 for missing/corrupt output, wrong units, invalid shape, critical geometry, or required parametricity; P1/P2 for secondary properties. Do not create several high-weight rows for the same underlying fact.

**Dependencies:** every deeper CAD check should depend on the file-existence/container check; task-specific dimensions should also depend on identity and units where appropriate.

**Negative case:** name a deliberately wrong artifact or mutation that must fail this row.

### **Which Studio verifier to use**

Use DB Code Verifier for static artifact checks that can be read safely from the FCStd ZIP, Document.xml, serialized properties, expressions, object tree, or embedded BREP records. In the row, fill Criteria, Criteria Explanation, Expected Content, Criterion Type \= Functional, Priority, Numerical Weight, and the approved verifier template variables. The criterion and explanation must describe the pass condition; the code must return the measured evidence and a clear failure reason.

Use the future Native FreeCAD verifier for opening, recomputing, Shape.isValid(), kernel-measured dimensions, bounds, area, volume, center of mass, inertia, topology, exportability, and mutation tests. Do not represent these as proven by a static DB Code Verifier.

Use an LLM or manual visual criterion only for qualities that are genuinely visual or communicative, such as drawing readability or an explicitly required presentation view. Do not use an LLM or screenshot comparison to establish exact geometry, units, mass, topology, parametricity, or shape validity.

### **Worked example: hypothetical parametric bracket**

**Row 1 \- File integrity (P0):** The delivered file filesystem/outputs/Mounting\_Bracket.FCStd exists, is non-empty, is a safe readable FCStd container, contains one Document.xml, and contains the required BREP payload. Negative case: corrupt or renamed ZIP.

**Row 2 \- Governing dimension** (P0, depends on Row 1): Spreadsheet alias Width equals 120.0 mm within \+/- 0.1 mm, as required by Drawing A-101, detail 3\. Negative case: Width \= 119.5 mm or units recorded as inches.

**Row 3 \- Parametric dependen**cy (P0, depends on Rows 1 and 2): the Width alias drives the named sketch constraint and the resulting PartDesign feature; the task fails if the model is a flattened Part::Feature with an unrelated custom property. Negative case: correct-looking static solid with no dependency path.

**Row 4 \- Native validity (P0, unavailable** until the native runtime is enabled): the pinned FreeCAD runtime opens and recomputes the exact output hash, Shape.isValid() is true, and the model contains the required number of solids. Negative case: broken reference or invalid/self-intersecting shape.

### **Rubric validation before submission**

Keep each row atomic and independently fail-able. Test the golden output against the current rubric after every rubric edit; an old 100% becomes stale when a criterion changes. Confirm that the golden passes, each negative fixture fails the intended row, failure messages identify the measured mismatch, and unrelated changes do not fail the row.

Finally, run one complete Studio trajectory using the same FreeCAD platform and grading configuration that experts will use. Confirm that the produced artifact is captured under the expected path and that grading reads the produced output rather than a world input, seed, screenshot, or local-only file.

# OTS specification

**OTS specification**  
Use this specification for tasks assigned to the OTS workstream. The Ergon requirements apply except for the three differences below. Where the guide gives conflicting requirements for step count, difficulty, or verifier type, this section takes precedence for OTS tasks.

**Step count**  
OTS tasks have no step-count requirement. The Ergon 100+ step requirement does not apply. Do not add steps or tool calls solely to increase the count.

**Difficulty**  
GPT Sol 5.6 must score less than 50% on the task rubric. This replaces the Ergon Gemini-based difficulty threshold for OTS tasks. Failures must reflect genuine reasoning or domain limitations, as described in the guide.

**Verifiers**  
OTS tasks must use DB diff LLM verifiers rather than programmatic verifiers. The LLM verifier evaluates the before-and-after database changes against the rubric criteria. Do not use App DB Programmatic verifiers for OTS tasks.
